privacy.title: Collaboration & Privacy
privacy.desc: Toggle for admins to view other users' data. Off by default.
privacy.viewOthersDesc: Once enabled, you can {readonly} view any user's sites in "User Management" (balance, check-in status, etc.; tokens are hidden). For admin troubleshooting only — you cannot edit, delete, scrape or check in.
privacy.term1: 1. This feature lets admins bypass data isolation to view other users' site data in read-only mode, only for troubleshooting, compliance audits and necessary operational support.
privacy.term2: 2. You must not use the data you view for any unauthorized purpose, including but not limited to forwarding, disclosure, commercial use or personal use.
privacy.term3: 3. This feature is read-only: the system does not allow editing, deleting, scraping, checking in or exporting others' data through this entry; sensitive fields (such as access tokens) are always hidden.
privacy.term4: 4. The backend records whether this permission is enabled (admin_global_view_ack); once turned off, the endpoints for viewing others' sites immediately go back to being rejected (returning 403).
privacy.term5: 5. As an admin you are responsible for your viewing actions and must comply with the data protection and privacy laws in your region. If you do not agree to the terms above, do not enable this feature.
privacy.agreeLabel: I have read and agree to the terms above, and understand this feature is only for read-only admin troubleshooting.
privacy.enableDesc: You must check the agreement above first. Turning it off revokes the permission.
privacy.needAgree: Please read the terms and check "I have read and agree" first
privacy.unlockedToast: Unlocked: you can view user sites in read-only mode
privacy.revokedToast: Revoked: others' sites are hidden again

activity.title: Health Check
activity.connectivityDesc: Test connection = the backend measures each site's {base}/api/pricing latency; channel test = send a probe word to each of the site's upstream models and check them one by one. All requests are made by the backend through the site-bound proxy (not subject to browser CORS).

activity.probeWordsDesc: The phrase sent to models during a channel test; a normal reply counts as alive. Bind a specific word to a site, or pick one as the global default; unbound sites use the global one.
activity.globalWordDesc: Sites without their own probe word use this by default. When turned off, those sites skip the channel test (connection test is unaffected).

scraper.settingsDesc: Global behavior of balance scraping; individual sites can override in their editor.

cf.title: Scraper · Cloudflare
cf.platformDesc: Scheduling is triggered by Cron Triggers (configured in wrangler.toml, not changeable at runtime on this page); self-hosted proxies are not supported, all requests go direct; limited by Workers' subrequest / CPU time, so keep concurrency low.
cf.autoScrapeDesc: Cloudflare Cron Triggers scrape periodically using the expression below.
cf.cronHint: Workers cron has a minimum granularity of 1 minute. This value is not hot-updated at runtime; write it into wrangler.toml and redeploy.
cf.proxyDesc: The Workers runtime cannot connect to self-hosted proxies (http/https/socks5 all unavailable); all sites go direct. Proxy support is available only in the Docker deployment.
cf.concurrencyHint: Constrained by the subrequest limit (50 free / 1000 paid per invocation); 6 or fewer is recommended, as too high easily hits the per-invocation quota.
cf.timeoutHint: Limited by Workers CPU time, the per-site timeout should not be too long (30 seconds or less recommended).

docker.title: Scraper · Docker
docker.platformDesc: Scheduling is driven by node-cron; the scrape interval can be changed anytime and takes effect immediately; supports http/https/socks5 outbound proxies (configured on the proxy page); concurrency / timeout / retry are freely configurable with no platform hard limits.
docker.autoScrapeDesc: node-cron periodically scrapes all sites' balances at the interval below.
docker.intervalHint: The minimum interval between two automatic scrapes; changes take effect immediately, no restart needed.
docker.proxyDesc: Supports http/https/socks5. Scraping/check-in go out through the proxy, managed centrally on the proxy page.
docker.concurrencyHint: Number of sites scraped simultaneously; no platform hard limit, but too high may still trigger site rate limiting.
docker.timeoutHint: A site request exceeding this duration is treated as failed.
docker.retryHint: Failed sites are retried with backoff this many times.

about.title: About Rrelaynest
about.subtitle: Balance and check-in management panel for relay stations.
about.scaleNote: By default it uses SQLite/D1 (single-file lock, serialized scheduling, per-request auth lookup), suitable for {scale}, each with dozens to hundreds of sites — small-scale personal use. For larger scale, upgrade to libSQL/Turso or Postgres (the business layer is already isolated; only the storage adapter changes).
about.noSelfUpdate: The app can't update itself; run the following steps in your deployment environment.
about.upgradeNoteWorkers: Workers must be rebuilt and redeployed; if GitHub auto-deploy is set up, pushing a tag publishes it automatically.
about.upgradeNoteDocker: Pull the latest image and rebuild the container; data volumes (SQLite / mounted directories) are preserved and unaffected.
about.viewReleaseNotes: View release notes for this version
about.autoCheckHint: Periodically checks GitHub Releases for new versions and shows them here. It never downloads or replaces anything automatically; you still upgrade manually.
